claim: Pathological metabolic conditions such as ischemia induce the rupture of the mitochondrial envelope and the release of pro-apoptotic proteins, leading to cell death.
source: Pathological metabolic conditions such as ischemia induce the rupture of the mitochondrial envelope and the release of pro-apoptotic proteins, leading to cell death.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about mitochondrial response to pathological conditions.

claim: At the onset of mitochondrial permeability transition, the inner mitochondrial membrane becomes depolarized and permeable to osmolytes.
source: At the onset of this process, the inner mitochondrial membrane becomes depolarized and permeable to osmolytes, proposedly due to the opening of a non-selective protein channel of unknown molecular identity.
evidence: This describes the proposed mechanism of MPTP based on existing literature.

claim: The depolarization and permeability of the inner mitochondrial membrane is proposedly due to the opening of a non-selective protein channel of unknown molecular identity.
source: At the onset of this process, the inner mitochondrial membrane becomes depolarized and permeable to osmolytes, proposedly due to the opening of a non-selective protein channel of unknown molecular identity.
evidence: This reflects the hypothesis in the field about MPTP mechanism.

claim: A recent study purports that the MPTP is formed within the c-subunit ring of the ATP synthase upon its dissociation from the catalytic domain of the enzyme.
source: A recent study purports that this channel, referred to as Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Pore (MPTP), is formed within the c-subunit ring of the ATP synthase, upon its dissociation from the catalytic domain of the enzyme.
evidence: This cites a specific claim from another study that is being investigated.

claim: The structure and biophysical properties of a correctly assembled c-ring are inconsistent with those attributed to the MPTP.
source: These calculations demonstrate that the structure and biophysical properties of a correctly assembled c-ring are inconsistent with those attributed to the MPTP.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by the computational data presented in the study.

claim: Under pathological conditions, mitochondria cease ATP production and instead trigger apoptosis.
source: Under certain pathological conditions mitochondria cease ATP production and instead trigger apoptosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mitochondrial function under stress.

claim: The depolarization of the inner mitochondrial membrane is at the onset of the apoptotic process.
source: At the onset of this process is the depolarization of the inner mitochondrial membrane, which under normal conditions sustains the proton-motive-force powering the ATP synthase.
evidence: This describes the sequence of events in mitochondrial apoptosis based on existing knowledge.

claim: Under normal conditions, the inner mitochondrial membrane sustains the proton-motive-force powering the ATP synthase.
source: At the onset of this process is the depolarization of the inner mitochondrial membrane, which under normal conditions sustains the proton-motive-force powering the ATP synthase.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ATP synthase function.

claim: It has long been hypothesized that membrane depolarization is mediated by a channel protein referred to as the MPTP.
source: It has long been hypothesized that this depolarization is mediated by a channel protein referred to as the Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Pore (MPTP) (Szabó and Zoratti, 1992; Bernardi and Forte, 2007; Halestrap, 2009; Azzolin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: The MPTP has very large ionic conductance (up to 1300 pS).
source: The hallmark properties of this putative channel are: very large ionic conductance (up to 1300 pS); high permeability to small molecules, including osmolytes (less than 1.5 kDa); and no solute specificity (aside from size-limit) or ion selectivity.
evidence: This describes the known properties of MPTP from literature.

claim: The MPTP has high permeability to small molecules, including osmolytes (less than 1.5 kDa).
source: The hallmark properties of this putative channel are: very large ionic conductance (up to 1300 pS); high permeability to small molecules, including osmolytes (less than 1.5 kDa); and no solute specificity (aside from size-limit) or ion selectivity.
evidence: This describes the known properties of MPTP from literature.

claim: The MPTP has no solute specificity (aside from size-limit) or ion selectivity.
source: The hallmark properties of this putative channel are: very large ionic conductance (up to 1300 pS); high permeability to small molecules, including osmolytes (less than 1.5 kDa); and no solute specificity (aside from size-limit) or ion selectivity.
evidence: This describes the known properties of MPTP from literature.

claim: Opening of the MPTP is thought to be induced by excessive amounts of Ca2+ or ROS in the mitochondrial matrix.
source: Thus, opening of the MPTP, thought to be induced, for example, by excessive amounts of Ca2+ or ROS in the mitochondrial matrix, is catastrophic for the cell
evidence: This reflects the hypothesis about MPTP activation from literature.

claim: Opening of the MPTP short-circuits the respiratory chain, causing the ATP synthase to reverse its activity and deplete cellular ATP.
source: not only does it short-circuit the respiratory chain, causing the ATP synthase to reverse its activity and deplete cellular ATP, but it also induces the osmotic swelling of the matrix, rupturing the outer membrane and causing the release of pro-apoptotic proteins (Halestrap, 2009).
evidence: This describes the consequences of MPTP opening based on cited literature.

claim: Opening of the MPTP induces the osmotic swelling of the matrix, rupturing the outer membrane and causing the release of pro-apoptotic proteins.
source: not only does it short-circuit the respiratory chain, causing the ATP synthase to reverse its activity and deplete cellular ATP, but it also induces the osmotic swelling of the matrix, rupturing the outer membrane and causing the release of pro-apoptotic proteins (Halestrap, 2009).
evidence: This describes the consequences of MPTP opening based on cited literature.

claim: The molecular identity of the MPTP remains to be established.
source: The molecular identity of the MPTP remains to be established.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Studies have implicated VDAC, ANT, and cyclophilin D as potential MPTP candidates, but none were found to be actually essential.
source: Seemingly promising studies have implicated mitochondrial proteins as diverse as the outer-membrane Voltage-Dependent Anion Channel (VDAC), the inner-membrane Adenine Nucleotide Translocase (ANT), and the non-transmembrane cyclophilin D; ultimately, however, none of these proteins was found to be actually essential (Bernardi and Forte, 2007; Halestrap, 2009; Azzolin et al., 2010; Bernardi et al., 2015).
evidence: This summarizes findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Jonas and co-workers have proposed that the c-ring is the MPTP.
source: More recently, Jonas and co-workers have proposed that a sub-complex of the mitochondrial F1Fo ATP synthase, known as the c-ring, is the MPTP (Alavian et al., 2014).
evidence: This cites a specific proposal from another research group.

claim: The c-ring is an oligomer of identical copies of subunit-c, each of which is a hairpin of two transmembrane helices.
source: The c-ring is an oligomer of identical copies of subunit-c, each of which is a hairpin of two transmembrane helices (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This describes the known structure of the c-ring with reference to a figure.

claim: When assembled, the c-ring helices are arranged in two concentric rings around a central lumen.
source: when assembled, these helices are arranged in two concentric rings around a central lumen (Meier et al., 2005; Pogoryelov et al., 2009; Symersky et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the structural arrangement based on cited studies.

claim: The F1 domain projects out of the membrane and contains the catalytic domain.
source: The F1 domain, which projects out of the membrane and contains the catalytic domain, sits atop the ring (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) (Dautant et al., 2010; Watt et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes the known structure and function of the F1 domain with citations.

claim: In the operating enzyme, the c-ring rotates against other static elements as protons sequentially bind to each of the c-subunits and are released across the membrane after a revolution.
source: In the operating enzyme, the membrane Fo domain works like a turbine, with the c-ring rotating against other static elements as protons sequentially bind to each of the c-subunits and are released across the membrane after a revolution (Meier et al., 2011; Leone and Faraldo-Gómez, 2016).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of ATP synthase based on cited literature.

claim: The proton-binding sites are on the outer surface of the c-ring and feature a conserved glutamate and other polar groups.
source: These proton-binding sites are on the outer surface of the ring, and feature a conserved glutamate and other polar groups (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Pogoryelov et al., 2009; Symersky et al., 2012; Vollmar et al., 2009; Zhou et al., 2016)
evidence: This describes the structural features of the c-ring based on multiple citations.

claim: The lumen of the c-ring is largely hydrophobic.
source: the lumen, by contrast, is largely hydrophobic.
evidence: This describes a structural property of the c-ring.

claim: Jonas et al. propose that metabolic conditions associated with the mitochondrial permeability transition induce the F1 and Fo sectors to dissociate, upon which the lumen of the c-ring would become the MPTP.
source: What Jonas et al. propose is that the metabolic conditions associated with the mitochondrial permeability transition induce the F1 and Fo sectors to dissociate, upon which the lumen of the c-ring would become the MPTP (Alavian et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the specific hypothesis being tested, citing the original proposal.

claim: The claim that the c-ring is the MPTP has been questioned by others.
source: Here, we use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to directly investigate the plausibility of this claim, which has been questioned by others (Bernardi et al., 2015; Halestrap, 2014).
evidence: This cites other researchers who have questioned the hypothesis.

claim: The c10-ring from Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the only mitochondrial c-ring of known atomic structure.
source: We first considered the c10-ring from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which is the only mitochondrial c-ring of known atomic structure (Figure 1A) (Symersky et al., 2012; Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about available structural data with citations.

claim: The lumen of the c10-ring is wider than that of the c8-rings found in vertebrates.
source: The lumen of this ring is also wider than that of the c8-rings found in vertebrates (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) (Watt et al., 2010)
evidence: This is a comparative structural observation based on cited data.

claim: The mitochondrial permeability transition has been observed in yeast.
source: (Note the mitochondrial permeability transition has also been observed in yeast (Azzolin et al., 2010)).
evidence: This cites experimental observations in yeast.

claim: The conductance of the c10-ring lumen is 2.5 pS for K+ and 116 pS for Cl− (for 100 mM KCl).
source: The resulting conductance values are 2.5 ps for K+ and 116 ps for Cl− (for 100 mM KCl).
evidence: These are calculated values from the molecular dynamics simulations presented in the study.

claim: The conductance values of the c10-ring are inconsistent with the properties of the MPTP in terms of magnitude and reveal marked anion selectivity.
source: These values are clearly inconsistent with the properties of the MPTP, not only in terms of their magnitude, but also in that they reveal a marked anion selectivity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the calculated conductance values to known MPTP properties.

claim: The anion selectivity of the c10-ring owes to a ring of arginine side-chains at the mouth of the lumen on the matrix side.
source: Analogous calculations carried out in the absence of electrolytes indicate that this selectivity owes to a ring of arginine side-chains at the mouth of the lumen, on the matrix side, which influences the energetics and dynamics of ion permeation electrostatically (Figure 1G and A).
evidence: This is an inference from computational experiments with and without electrolytes.

claim: The electropositive arginine ring is conserved in other mitochondrial c-rings.
source: This electropositive arginine ring, which is conserved in other mitochondrial c-rings (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is a structural observation based on sequence/structure comparison.

claim: The arginine ring counters the cost of dehydration for Cl− but imposes an additional barrier for K+.
source: counters the cost of dehydration for Cl-−, but imposes an additional barrier for K+ (Figure 1C), incompatible with the high conductance properties of the MPTP.
evidence: This is an inference from the free energy profiles calculated in the simulations.

claim: The water-filled state of the c10-ring lumen is approximately 15 kcal/mol less favorable than a state in which most of the lumen is void of water.
source: However, this water-filled state is approximately 15 kcal/mol less favorable than a second state in which most of the lumen of the c-ring is void of any water (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the metadynamics free energy calculations.

claim: The probability that the c-ring lumen exists in a 'conducting state' is negligible.
source: That is, the probability that the c-ring lumen exists in a 'conducting state' is negligible – a dehydrated, non-conducting state is much more probable, by multiple orders of magnitude.
evidence: This is an inference from the free energy difference calculated in the simulations.

claim: The notion that the c-ring is the MPTP implicitly assumes that lipid molecules are excluded from its lumen as c-subunits assemble.
source: Irrespective of the question of hydration, the notion that the c-ring is the MPTP implicitly assumes that lipid molecules are somehow excluded from its lumen as c-subunits gradually assemble to form a ring.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the assumptions underlying the MPTP hypothesis.

claim: There is no evidence that lipid molecules are excluded from the c-ring lumen during assembly.
source: There is, however, no evidence that this is the case
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of supporting evidence in the literature.

claim: Detergent molecules are often observed in the lumen in X-ray structures of c-rings.
source: to the contrary, detergent molecules are often observed in the lumen in X-ray structures of c-rings (Pogoryelov et al., 2010; Schulz et al., 2013; Matthies et al., 2014)
evidence: This cites structural evidence from multiple X-ray crystallography studies.

claim: AFM images of two-dimensional ring arrays indicate the lumen might be occluded.
source: and AFM images of two-dimensional ring arrays also indicate the lumen might be occluded (Meier et al., 2001).
evidence: This cites AFM imaging evidence.

claim: In three independent simulations of the c10-ring lacking two c-subunits, water is quickly displaced by lipid molecules entering the lumen.
source: As shown in Figure 3A–C, however, the three simulations consistently demonstrate that all this water is quickly displaced by lipid molecules gradually entering the c-ring lumen
evidence: This describes the results from molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: Lipid molecules ultimately occupy the totality of the c-ring lumen in a bilayer-like arrangement.
source: ultimately, these lipid molecules occupy the totality of the pore, in a bilayer-like arrangement akin to that outside the c-ring (Figure 3C).
evidence: This describes the final state observed in the simulations.

claim: There is no reason to assume that incorporation of the two missing c-subunits would alter the lipid occupancy of the lumen.
source: There is no reason to assume that the incorporation of the two missing c-subunits would alter the lipid occupancy of the lumen, which would therefore remain in a non-conducting state when the c-ring assembles completely.
evidence: This is an inference from the simulation results about the complete ring.

claim: Subtle variations in the amino-acid sequence of the c-subunits can destabilize the native state of a c-ring and favor the assembly of larger c-rings.
source: This expansion is not entirely implausible; indeed, subtle variations in the amino-acid sequence of the c-subunits can destabilize the native state of a c-ring, and favor the assembly of larger c-rings with a slightly greater number of c-subunits (Pogoryelov et al., 2012).
evidence: This cites experimental evidence about c-ring assembly.

claim: The c13-ring from Bacillus pseudofirmus features the widest lumen among ATP synthase c-rings of known structure.
source: Among the ATP synthase c-rings of known structure, this specific c13-ring features the widest lumen (Preiss et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparative structural observation based on cited data.

claim: No process akin to the permeability transition has been described in bacteria.
source: Thus, although no process akin to the permeability transition has been described in bacteria
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of reported phenomena in bacteria.

claim: Because the c13-ring lumen is wider, the permeability of the hydrated state is significantly larger, but this state remains highly anion-selective.
source: Because the lumen is wider, the permeability of the hydrated state is significantly larger, but this state remains highly anion-selective (Figure 1H), unlike the MPTP.
evidence: This describes the calculated results for the c13-ring variant.

claim: The water-filled state of the c13-ring is still disfavored relative to the empty lumen, albeit to a lesser degree than in the c10-ring.
source: Moreover, this water-filled state is still disfavored, relative to the empty lumen, albeit to a lesser degree than in the c10-ring (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This describes the free energy calculation results for the c13-ring.

claim: Independent simulations of a c13-ring assembly intermediate lacking two c-subunits demonstrate that the preferred state is one in which lipid molecules occlude the lumen in a bilayer arrangement.
source: Importantly, though, independent simulations of an assembly intermediate lacking two c-subunits demonstrate that the preferred state is again one in which lipid molecules occlude the lumen, in a bilayer arrangement (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This describes the simulation results for the c13-ring assembly intermediate.

claim: The characteristics of the lumen of the mitochondrial c-ring are incompatible with the conducting properties of the MPTP.
source: This study demonstrates that the characteristics of the lumen of the mitochondrial c-ring are incompatible with the conducting properties of the MPTP.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the computational data presented.

claim: The F1 domain does not actually seal the entrance to the lumen of the c-ring in the fully assembled, operating enzyme.
source: Consistent with the fact that the F1 domain does not actually seal the entrance to the lumen of the c-ring in the fully assembled, operating enzyme (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is a structural observation from known structures.

claim: The interior of the c-ring is not water-filled, but occupied by lipid molecules in a non-conducting state.
source: the interior of the ring is not water-filled, but occupied by lipid molecules; that is, it is in a non-conducting state, thereby precluding the dissipation of the ion-motive-force that powers ATP synthesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the simulation data about the preferred state of the lumen.

claim: Even if the c-ring became dissociated from the F1 domain and its lumen became hydrated, the conductance levels sustained would be unlike those of the MPTP.
source: Our results also show that even if the c-ring became dissociated from the F1 domain (Alavian et al., 2014), despite the nanomolar affinity of this interaction (Pogoryelov et al., 2008), and even if its lumen was to become hydrated, under some hypothetical in vitro conditions, the conductance levels sustained by the c-ring would be unlike those of the MPTP.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the conductance calculations presented in the study.

claim: The F1-Fo interaction has nanomolar affinity.
source: despite the nanomolar affinity of this interaction (Pogoryelov et al., 2008)
evidence: This cites experimental measurements of binding affinity.

claim: This study does not rule out that an as-yet-unknown molecular structure consisting of c-subunits, distinct from that of the c-ring, matches the properties of the MPTP.
source: Admittedly, this study does not rule out that an as-yet-unknown molecular structure consisting of c-subunits, distinct from that of the c-ring, matches the properties of the MPTP.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the study's scope.

claim: No evidence of an alternative c-subunit structure exists.
source: However, it is also worth noting that no evidence of such alternative structure exists, to our knowledge.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of evidence in the literature.

claim: Structural studies of the c-subunit and its oligomers date back two decades.
source: Structural studies of the c-subunit and its oligomers date back two decades
evidence: This is a statement about the history of research in the field.

claim: Across a wide variety of species and experimental conditions, the consistent conclusion is that c-subunits assemble in ring-like oligomers.
source: Across a wide variety of species and experimental conditions, the consistent conclusion from these studies is that the c-subunits assemble in ring-like oligomers such as those analyzed here.
evidence: This summarizes the consensus from multiple structural studies.

claim: The ring-like oligomer conclusion holds true for wild-type, mutagenized and inhibited forms of the c-ring, and for a variety of expression systems.
source: This conclusion holds true for wild-type, mutagenized and inhibited forms of the c-ring, and for a variety of expression systems (including cell-free).
evidence: This describes the breadth of experimental conditions supporting the structural consensus.

claim: No apparent discrepancy exists between structural data and biochemical and functional measurements for the ATP synthase.
source: Moreover, to our knowledge no apparent discrepancy exists between this set of structural data and the even larger collection of biochemical and functional measurements gathered for this enzyme or its constituent elements.
evidence: This is a statement about the consistency of different types of experimental data.

claim: Thermodynamic data on Na+/H+ binding to isolated c-rings is quantitatively consistent with kinetic measurements for the complete enzyme functioning in membranes.
source: Indeed, in the instances where clear thermodynamic data has been attained, for example, on Na+/H+ binding to isolated c-rings, it was found to be not only quantitatively consistent with kinetic measurements for the complete enzyme functioning in membranes, but also explicable based on existing structures and theoretical considerations (Murata et al., 2008; Leone et al., 2015).
evidence: This cites specific examples of consistent experimental data.

claim: In absence of concrete experimental evidence of an alternative architecture, the logical conclusion is that the c-ring from the mitochondrial ATP synthase is not the MPTP.
source: In absence of concrete experimental evidence of the existence of an alternative architecture, the logical conclusion from this body of work and the present study is therefore that the c-ring from the mitochondrial ATP synthase is not the MPTP.
evidence: This is the final conclusion drawn from the computational results and literature review.

claim: The computational framework used produces conductance values that are in good agreement with experimental measurements.
source: It is important to note that this computational framework has been shown to produce conductance values that are in good agreement with experimental measurements (Zhu and Hummer, 2012).
evidence: This validates the computational method by citing previous benchmarking work.

claim: The water-filled state of the c-ring lumen is metastable and sufficiently long-lived to observe tens of permeation events.
source: (It was not required to impose this condition, as this state is metastable and sufficiently long-lived to observe tens of permeation events).
evidence: This describes an observation from the molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: Open c-ring assembly intermediates lacking two c-subunits have been observed in AFM micrographs of prokaryotic c-rings.
source: This open c-ring resembles the kind of assembly intermediate that has been observed in AFM micrographs of prokaryotic c-rings (Müller et al., 2001; Pogoryelov et al., 2005).
evidence: This cites AFM imaging studies of c-ring assembly.
